## Scope

This vignette describes the classification case-study protocol: generation,
target selection, numerical reconstruction and evaluation. Building this
vignette does not execute the case-study experiments.

## Reference and holdout

The study uses 9,000 real training records and a separate 1,000-record real
holdout. Diagnosis is the categorical response. The eight variables are age,
gender, civil status, occupation, physical activity, genetic predisposition,
municipality of residence and diagnosis. Age is discretized for generation and
fidelity and reconstructed within its original saved bin after landing.
Municipality of residence is the highest-cardinality conditioning variable.

The holdout is not used to fit the BN, the plausibility discriminator, the
association-selection forests or the landing utility guide. Final external
predictive comparisons use this same real holdout.

## Approved flight and landing

The approved flight uses six chains, BN proposals and plausibility, privacy and
chain-local diversity energy terms. Duplicate synthetic record contents are
retained. The approved landing selects 9,000 pool indices using one million
single-record swap proposals. Its objective is mean categorical fidelity plus
absolute fixed-RF accuracy gap, with coefficient one for each term. There is no
additional diversity term in this landing.

The fidelity components include all eight marginals, seven distributions
conditioned on municipality, and these five bivariate distributions:

- age and civil status;
- age and occupation;
- age and genetic predisposition;
- diagnosis and physical activity;
- genetic predisposition and diagnosis.

The twenty components receive equal weight in their arithmetic mean. Conditional
discrepancies use real municipality proportions. This is the approved protocol,
not earlier maximum-based or adaptive-weight variants.

## Final numerical release

Only the corrected age reconstruction is used for final audits: applying the
saved discretizer to reconstructed ages must reproduce every selected age bin.
The selected categorical records are unchanged by this correction. Older
releases with age-bin crossings must not be mixed with the corrected outputs.
Final-release duplicates and exact matches are measured after reconstruction;
duplicates are reported, not removed.

## Fidelity, privacy and stability

Fidelity is assessed on selected categorical records and on the final numerical
release. Privacy checks include exact matches, duplicates, nearest-neighbour
features and membership attacks with separate attack training, calibration and
test sets. Repeated membership splits reuse the same release and candidate
features; they are not independent synthetic-data replications.

The target stability experiment generates ten targets from the same fixed pool,
with different landing seeds and valid numerical reconstruction. It measures
variation due to target selection and reconstruction, not variation in flight.
The existing completed results are retained; documentation work does not require
running these experiments again.

## External utility

XT, bagged CART and XGB are fitted to each of the ten final targets with one
fixed model seed and the same model configuration. Each model is also fitted
once to the real training reference. All fits are evaluated on the same 1,000
real holdout records: thirty synthetic fits and three real baselines.

Accuracy and probabilistic metrics answer different questions and must be
reported separately. Repeated targets evaluated against a shared holdout do not
provide independent test datasets. The case study validates a classification
application; it does not provide empirical validation of the continuous-response
extension.

## Reproducibility

Reproduction uses the original training/holdout split, saved discretizers,
model settings, seeds and software versions. Final audits use the corrected
numerical release and the approved categorical selection. Preserve these inputs
and the saved result tables together. A new generalized workflow call need not
be bitwise identical to an earlier script run under another software environment.

## Included inputs

The original CSV files are installed under `extdata/paper`. Their checksums and
observed variable inventory accompany them. Read all columns as character first
and convert age to integer; the diagnosis codes represent classes.

```{r load-inputs}
folder <- system.file("extdata", "paper", package="SPADES.IND")
training <- read.csv(file.path(folder, "training_data.csv"),
                     colClasses="character", na.strings=NULL)
holdout <- read.csv(file.path(folder, "test_real_1000.csv"),
                    colClasses="character", na.strings=NULL)
training$age <- as.integer(training$age)
holdout$age <- as.integer(holdout$age)
stopifnot(nrow(training)==9000L, nrow(holdout)==1000L)
```

The supplied training CSV includes literal `Missing` categories in physical
activity and genetic predisposition. Preserve the original files for provenance.
If these labels are declared missing when preparing an analysis, complete-case
filtering changes the reference and must be reported explicitly. The installed
`extdata/paper/README.md` describes the input conventions. Historical fitted
models and approved result tables are separate from these input files.
